**Finding submitted: `needs_review` (no redline proposed).**

**What the document actually contains.** The only liability-allocation language is Article 11:
- **§ 11.5 (p0572)** — a mutual, all-caps waiver of indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive and consequential damages, with mutual carve-outs for **fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence**, breach of **Article 9 (Confidentiality) or § 5.8**, and third-party damages payable under an **Article 11 indemnity**.
- **§§ 11.1/11.2 (p0559–p0560)** — mutual indemnities, with no monetary ceiling.
- **§ 11.6** — insurance minimums (not a cap).

Searches across "aggregate liability", "shall not exceed", "limitation of liability", "maximum liability", "no event shall", "liable", "damages" and "Losses" confirm **no aggregate monetary cap exists anywhere**. The only "maximum aggregate" figures are Article 6 milestone payment ceilings, not liability caps.

**Why needs_review rather than deviation.** The four fallback carve-out elements are met on the face of § 11.5 (and, absent any cap, are uncapped in fact). The two cap elements are genuinely unmet — but the regime is **fully symmetric**: neither AbbVie's nor Harpoon's direct liability is limited, so no walk-away trigger (our liability capped-out while Vendor's is capped, sub-6-month Vendor cap, indemnities inside a cap) is present. Importing a 12-month-fees cap would, for the first time, **cap Harpoon's exposure to us** and cut off recovery under the § 11.2 indemnity and Article 10 warranties — a weakening of our position I declined to draft. It also has no workable basis: consideration here is an upfront/option payment, milestones and royalties, not recurring fees.

**Escalation note for the deal team.** If the business wants an outer limit on our own uncapped § 11.1 indemnity exposure, ask for a mutual cap measured as a percentage of amounts paid or payable by AbbVie, with § 11.5's existing carve-outs (plus IP infringement and AbbVie's payment obligations) expressly outside it.
